title: Computer Systems
tagline: Bits and integers, floating point, C, machine-level programs, the memory hierarchy, linking, processes, dynamic memory and system-level input and output
summary: Every program ultimately runs as machine instructions on real hardware, and knowing how makes programs faster, safer and easier to debug. This course follows a program from C source to a running process: how data are represented in bits, the C language and its memory model, x86-64 machine code, the memory hierarchy and caches, linking and loading, exceptional control flow and processes, dynamic memory allocation and system-level input and output.

chapters.title: Bits, bytes and integers
chapters.summary: Binary and hexadecimal, unsigned and two’s-complement integers, bitwise operations and integer overflow.

chapters.title: Floating point
chapters.summary: IEEE 754 representation, rounding, special values and the pitfalls of floating-point arithmetic.

chapters.title: Programming in C
chapters.summary: Types, pointers and arrays, structures, the stack and the heap, and undefined behaviour.

chapters.title: Machine-level programs
chapters.summary: x86-64 instructions and registers, control flow and procedure calls, and how C compiles to assembly.

chapters.title: The memory hierarchy and caches
chapters.summary: Locality, cache organisation and performance, and writing cache-friendly code.

chapters.title: Linking and loading
chapters.summary: Object files, symbol resolution and relocation, and static and shared libraries.

chapters.title: Exceptional control flow and processes
chapters.summary: Interrupts, traps and system calls, processes, fork and exec, and signals.

chapters.title: Dynamic memory allocation
chapters.summary: The heap, malloc and free, allocator design, fragmentation, and memory errors such as leaks and use-after-free.

chapters.title: System-level input and output
chapters.summary: File descriptors, Unix input and output, buffering, and how the standard library sits on system calls.
